**Analysis date: 2026-11-24 | Last close: $161.18 | Exchange: NMS | Classification: Technology / Software – Infrastructure**

---

## 1. Executive Read

PLTR is in the middle of a **two-speed trend conflict** that has been running since October:

- **Long-term structure is still constructive.** The 200-day SMA sits at **$154.18** and is *rising*. Price closed above it on 2026-11-23 for the first time since a two-day breach on 11/19–11/20, and held above it on 11/24.
- **Intermediate structure is decisively negative.** The 50-day SMA at **$182.75** is *falling*, and price is **11.8% below it**. The 50 is rolling over from above.
- **Short-term structure has just inflected.** Price closed above the 10-day EMA (**$160.04**) on 11/24 for the **first time in 18 trading sessions** (since 2026-10-27), and above the volume-weighted average (**$160.18**).

The 11/20–11/24 move is a violent oversold relief rally (+12.33% off the 11/20 close of $143.49), but it is **not yet volume-confirmed** — 11/24 traded only 20.56M shares versus a ~24.5M 30-session average, and the day itself had a range of just $5.21 (3.2%), roughly **half of one ATR**. This is a *pause* in the bounce, not an expansion of it.

**Bottom line:** PLTR is bouncing off a genuine long-term support zone (200-day + unfilled gap), but the tape is not yet confirming a trend reversal. Treat this as a **tactical long only with tight risk**, until the MACD histogram crosses zero and the $168–176 supply shelf is cleared on real volume.

---

## 2. Indicator Selection — Why These 8

I selected a set that separates *trend*, *timing*, *momentum regime*, and *risk*, without stacking redundant readings:

| Indicator | Role in this setup | Why it earns its place |
|---|---|---|
| `close_200_sma` | Regime anchor | The line in the sand for the long-term uptrend; was just undercut and reclaimed |
| `close_50_sma` | Intermediate trend filter | Quantifies the overhead supply and the post-golden-cross decay |
| `close_10_ema` | Tactical trigger | Reclaim is the cleanest short-term timing signal available |
| `macd` | Momentum regime (level) | Establishes MACD is *below zero* — the move is a bounce inside a downtrend, not a new trend |
| `macdh` | Momentum inflection (timing) | Histogram is the crossover clock; shows bearish momentum decaying at maximum rate right now |
| `rsi` | Stretch & divergence | Identifies the oversold conditions that drove the bounce and shows room to run |
| `atr` | Volatility & sizing | ATR expanded ~49% since early October; directly dictates stop distance and position size |
| `vwma` | Volume-weighted confirmation | Tests whether *volume-supported* money is on the buyers' side, not just price |

**Deliberately excluded for redundancy:** `macds` (the MACD signal line is mathematically embedded in `macdh` — `macdh = macd − macds`, so adding it yields no new information); `boll` (a 20-day SMA, redundant with the MA stack); `stochrsi`-style duplicates of `rsi`.

**Supplementary note:** I also pulled the Bollinger envelope (`boll_ub` $195.42 / `boll_lb` $140.53, middle $167.97) from the verified snapshot as a **context check only** — it is used below to frame the range geometry and mean-reversion reference, not as a ninth trigger. Every Bollinger figure quoted is from the snapshot.

**Tool reconciliation:** All eight selected indicators agree with `get_verified_market_snapshot` to rounding (10 EMA 160.038 vs 160.04; 50 SMA 182.754 vs 182.75; 200 SMA 154.177 vs 154.18; RSI 43.170 vs 43.17; MACD −8.486 vs −8.49; ATR 9.420 vs 9.42). No conflicts to flag. `vwma` is supplied only by the indicator tool (160.176) and is not in the snapshot; its period is not documented by the vendor, so I treat it as a vendor-computed volume-weighted mean without asserting a lookback length.

---

## 3. Trend Structure — Three Timeframes Disagreeing

### 3.1 Long-term: uptrend intact, and the golden cross is still alive

The 50-day crossed **above** the 200-day on **2026-09-09** (50 SMA $152.11 vs 200 SMA $151.41). That golden cross is still intact today at $182.75 vs $154.18. Critically, the 200-day is **still rising** — from $151.37 on 2026-09-04 to $154.18 on 2026-11-24 — which is the single most important fact for anyone holding longs through this drawdown.

But the gap between them is **collapsing**: 50 SMA has fallen from $186.87 (11/02) to $182.75, and it is falling roughly 4–6 points/week while price is ~$21 below it. That configuration — price below a rolling-over 50, above a rising 200 — is the classic post-golden-cross correction.

**The 200-day is the decision point.** It was breached on 11/19 (close $153.68 vs SMA $153.90) and 11/20 (close $143.49 vs SMA $153.97), then reclaimed on 11/23 ($159.36 vs $154.09) and 11/24 ($161.18 vs $154.18). Two closes of confirmation in under two days.

### 3.2 The gap structure (the most actionable detail in this report)

The 11/20 session gapped **down** sharply: open $149.70 vs 11/19 close $153.68, low $142.28, close $143.49. The 11/23 session then gapped **up**: open $157.32 vs 11/20 close $143.49, low $154.57, close $159.36.

That creates an **unfilled gap-down zone of $143.49 → $154.57**. Price has not traded back into it. And the 200-day SMA at **$154.18 sits precisely at the upper boundary of that gap zone**.

This is the highest-quality confluence on the chart: **$153–155 is simultaneously (a) the rising 200-day, (b) the top of the unfilled Nov-23 gap, and (c) the 11/05 capitulation close of $154.99.** A pullback into that band that holds is the highest-quality long entry on the chart. A decisive close below it confirms the gap fill and the failure of the bounce.

*(Note the mirror image: the 11/05 gap-down from $171.70 to $166.71 was fully filled on 11/09, when the high reached $170.83.)*

### 3.3 Intermediate: unequivocally bearish

Price is **11.8% below** the 50-day SMA ($161.18 vs $182.75). The decline itself was textbook lower-highs: $209.00 (10/12) → $171.70 (11/04) → $167.99 (11/13) → $143.49 (11/20).

From the 2026 closing high of **$209.00 (2026-10-12)** to the 11/20 close of $143.49, PLTR lost **31.34%** in 26 trading sessions. That is a full bear-market-grade correction, and it is why the oscillator conditions and volume profile look the way they do now.

### 3.4 Short-term: a genuine flip, but a one-day-old one

| Date | Close | 10 EMA | Position vs EMA |

| 11/19 | 153.68 | 163.52 | −6.0% |
| 11/20 | 143.49 | 159.88 | −10.3% |
| 11/23 | 159.36 | 159.78 | −0.3% |
| **11/24** | **161.18** | **160.04** | **+0.7%** |

The 10-EMA slope is still negative (it was $180.12 on 11/05), so the EMA itself is not confirming — price has merely closed above a still-falling average. That is a classic **oversold mean-reversion pop**, not a trend change. The 10 EMA will need ~5–7 more sessions of higher closes to flatten and then turn up.

---

## 4. Momentum — Divided Signals

### 4.1 MACD: below zero, but the histogram is screaming "inflection"

- **MACD line: −8.49** — below zero, having crossed from +0.55 on 11/02 to −0.85 on 11/03. Price momentum is still in negative territory.
- **Signal line: −7.74**
- **Histogram: −0.75** — *still negative* (no bullish crossover yet) but **improving sharply**.

The histogram trajectory is the single most bullish element in this report:

| Date | Histogram |
|---|---|
| 11/06 | −5.03 |
| 11/09 | −4.27 |
| 11/12 | −2.04 |
| 11/16 | −1.85 |
| 11/20 | **−2.49** (the capitulation spike) |
| 11/23 | −1.58 |
| **11/24** | **−0.75** |

Bearish momentum decayed from −5.03 to −0.75 — an **85% compression** — in 13 sessions. The MACD line itself has risen three straight sessions: −9.64 (11/20) → −9.13 (11/23) → −8.49 (11/24). **The MACD line needs to climb just ~0.75 to cross above its signal line**, which would be the first bullish MACD crossover since the histogram last turned positive on 2026-10-14 (+1.04). Until that print lands, the bounce remains a counter-trend move inside a negative-momentum regime.

### 4.2 RSI: recovering from genuine oversold, with room to run

**RSI = 43.17** (11/24), up from **26.38 on 11/20** and **25.42 on 11/05**.

Two readings below 30 within six weeks, and the earlier one has a clean precedent: **after RSI printed 25.42 on 2026-11-05 (close $154.99), PLTR rallied to $172.40 by 11/11 — +11.2% in four sessions.** The current setup is analogous.

Two important qualifications:

1. **RSI at 43.17 is below the neutral 50 line** — momentum has recovered from oversold but has *not* yet returned to positive territory. This is the definition of a bounce, not a reversal, until it clears 50.
2. **There is a mild positive divergence** worth tracking: price printed a materially lower low on 11/20 ($143.49 vs $154.99 on 11/05), yet RSI bottomed at 26.38 vs 25.42 — *higher* on the lower price low. The margin is slim (0.96 points), so I treat this as a **weak, developing** divergence rather than a confirmed one. It becomes meaningful if RSI holds above 30 on any subsequent pullback.

For context on how frothy this name gets: RSI printed **76.29 on 2026-10-09** and **76.20 on 2026-10-12** at the exact peak ($209.00 close, $212.94 intraday high). **Every reading on the current bounce — a peak of 43.17 — is in the shadow of that.** There is no overbought risk whatsoever.

---

## 5. Volatility — The Regime Has Changed Materially

**ATR = $9.42** (5.84% of the $161.18 close). Compare:

| Date | ATR | Implied daily range |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-01 | $6.25 | 3.3% |
| 2026-10-14 | $6.77 | 3.4% |

| 2026-11-23 | $9.74 | 6.1% |
| **2026-11-24** | **$9.42** | **5.8%** |

ATR has expanded **~51%** since early October. **PLTR is no longer the same instrument traders were positioning in September.** Any position sized on the old $6 ATR is now roughly 1.5x oversized in risk terms.

Two constructive nuances: ATR ticked *down* from $9.74 on 11/23 to $9.42 on 11/24, and 11/24's actual range was only $5.21 (high $163.01 − low $157.80) — less than one ATR. **Volatility is compressing slightly even as price holds above the 200-day**, which is consistent with a stabilizing market rather than a fresh panic.

**Bollinger context (from the verified snapshot):**

- Band width = **32.7%** of the middle line — versus roughly 19.5% on 2026-10-10. Bands have widened by more than half, quantifying the volatility regime shift.
- **%B = 37.6%** — price sits in the lower half of the envelope, but is no longer near the lower band.
- The **upper band is falling fast** ($220.16 on 11/05 → $195.42 on 11/24) — the mean is being dragged down, which confirms the intermediate trend is still deteriorating even as the oscillator recovers.
- The **middle band at $167.97** is the near-term mean-reversion target and is a confluence with the Nov 11–12 closes ($172.40, $171.58).

---

## 6. Volume — The Weak Link

The bounce is **not volume-confirmed**, and this is the most important caveat in the report.

Three observations:

1. **The 11/23 bounce day was +11.06% on 32.07M shares** — that is respectable participation, but it is *less* than the 41.87M/37.62M that drove the October advance, and far less than the 175.03M that powered the 2026-08-04 breakout. Bounces on declining volume are typically short-covering, not accumulation.
2. **The 11/24 follow-through printed only 20.56M**, below the ~24.5M 30-session average. Institutions were not adding on the second leg.
3. **VWMA = $160.18.** Price closed at $161.18 — only $1.00 above the volume-weighted average, and the VWMA is *still falling* (from $199.38 on 10/27, a ~19.7% collapse). Reclaiming a still-descending VWMA is the **earliest** possible confirmation. Until the VWMA flattens and turns up, the volume-weighted position of traders is still net short.

**Notably, the 10 EMA ($160.04) and VWMA ($160.18) are within 14 cents of each other.** This creates a genuine **$160 decision cluster**. Price is sitting on top of it. A close below $160 opens the gap toward the 200-day; a sustained hold above it with expanding volume is the trigger for a higher target.

## 8. Actionable Scenarios

### Scenario A — Bull Continuation (probability: moderate; requires volume confirmation)

**Trigger:** Daily close above **$167.97** (Bollinger middle) *with* volume ≥ 30M shares, **and** the MACD histogram crossing to positive (MACD line must close above ~$−7.74 and then breach zero).

**Targets:**
- T1: $171.58–$172.40 (11/11–11/12 closes) — +6.5% to +7.0%
- T2: $175.40 (11/03 close / gap top) — +8.8%
- T3: $182.75 (50 SMA) — +13.4%
- T4: $195.42 (upper band) — +21.2%
- T5: $209.00 (2026 high close) — +29.6%

**T1 is the realistic first target; T3 is the "trend actually changed" target.** Take partials at T1 and T2; only hold for T4+ if the 50 SMA gets reclaimed on a closing basis.

**Risk:** Below $160, the breakout is suspect. Below $154.18, it is void.

### Scenario B — Range / Chop (probability: highest; this is the base case)

Price oscillates between the 200-day ($154.18) and the Bollinger middle band ($167.97), with the MACD histogram hovering just below zero while ATR compresses toward ~$7–8.

**Play:** This is the highest-expected-value environment for mean-reversion, but it punishes trend-followers. Use smaller size (half normal), respect the $153–155 and $168–170 boundaries as fade levels, and do not chase the middle of the range. Tighten trailing stops toward the 10 EMA / VWMA cluster at $160 as long as you hold.

### Scenario C — Bear Resumption (probability: real; the volume data argues for it)

**Trigger:** Close below **$154.18** (200-day) — which means a fill of the $143.49–$154.57 gap zone — *on volume expansion* (≥35M).

**Targets:**
- T1: $143.49 / $142.28 (11/20 close / low) — −11.0%
- T2: $140.53 (lower band) — −12.8%
- T3: $130.01 (2026-02-05 close) — −19.4%
- T4: $128.06 / $122.68 (2026-04-10 close / low) — −20.6% / −23.9%
- T5: $107.27 / $106.37 (2026-06-25 close / low, the 2026 low) — −33.5% / −34.0%

**Invalidation of the bear case:** Hold above $154.18 on any retest and reclaim $167.97.

**Note the asymmetry:** downside to $140.53 is −12.8% from spot; upside to the 50 SMA ($182.75) is +13.4%. Roughly symmetric — but the *next* tranche of downside ($130) is far larger than the next tranche of upside ($195) sits... actually at $195 the upside is +21.2%. The point stands that this is a **two-sided, high-volatility range**, and leverage should be sized to survive either resolution.

---

## 9. Risk Management Framework

With ATR at $9.42, stops must be ATR-derived, not percentage-derived:

| Entry | Stop | Distance | ATR multiple | R:R to $182.75 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $161.18 | $150.00 (below 200-day + gap zone) | $11.18 (6.9%) | 1.19 ATR | 1.93 : 1 |
| $161.18 | $140.00 (below 11/20 low & lower band) | $21.18 (13.1%) | 2.25 ATR | 1.02 : 1 |

**Sizing:** With ATR expanded ~51% since early October, **cut position size by roughly one-third to one-half** versus what the same dollar risk supported in September.

- At a $150 stop (6.9% risk): a 1% account risk supports ~14.5% of equity.
- At a $140 stop (13.1% risk): a 1% account risk supports ~7.6% of equity.

**Prefer the tighter $150 stop** for the tactical swing — the structure supports it because the 200-day, the gap-zone top, and the 11/05 capitulation close all cluster at $153–155. If that band fails on a closing basis, the tight stop is *supposed* to take you out. Don't widen it.

**Volume-confirmation filter is mandatory.** Do not add to this position on a close below 20M shares; that signature (as on 11/24) is the tell that the bounce is running on air.

---

## 10. What Would Falsify This Read

I would be wrong to stay bullish if:
1. The **200-day SMA ($154.18)** fails on a closing basis with expanding volume — the long-term uptrend premise is broken.
2. The **MACD histogram** rolls back down from −0.75 toward −2.00+ without price making new lows — that would be bearish momentum re-accelerating, invalidating the "decelerating bear" thesis.
3. The **RSI bullish divergence** fails — RSI closing back below 30 after touching 43.17 would confirm the bounce as a lower-high in momentum.
4. **VWMA ($160.18)** keeps falling and price loses it — volume-weighted traders remain net short, and the bounce has no institutional sponsorship.

Conversely, I'd turn more constructive if: price holds above $160 for 3+ sessions, the histogram prints positive, and $167.97 clears on ≥30M shares.

**Palantir Technologies Inc.** was founded in 2003/2004 by Peter Thiel, Alex Karp, Joe Lonsdale and Stephen Cohen; it went public via direct listing on the NYSE on 2020-09-30 (no traditional underwritten IPO). It is headquartered in Denver, Colorado, and operates a **multi-class share structure** (Class A, Class B, Class F) with founder-controlled supervoting rights — a governance feature that materially reduces the risk of hostile influence but concentrates decision-making.

**Segment architecture (as reported by the company):**
- **Government / Gotham** — long-standing counterterrorism, intelligence and defense missions; the original business and the source of the durable, contract-backed revenue base.
- **Commercial / Foundry** — enterprise operational data platforms for manufacturing, healthcare, logistics, energy and financial services.
- **AIP (Artificial Intelligence Platform)** — the highest-growth vector and the strategic center of gravity. AIP overlays large language models and machine-learning workflows onto Foundry/Gotham's ontology layer, sold largely through "bootcamps" that convert proofs-of-concept into production contracts.
- **Apollo** — the continuous-delivery/edge deployment layer enabling on-prem, air-gapped and sovereign deployments, which is a major driver of the US government and allied-government business.

**Economic model:** Enterprise software / platform subscription-and-usage hybrid. Very high gross margin (now ~84% and historically ~80%), negligible capital intensity (capex <1% of revenue), and a large deferred-revenue/contract-liability base that gives revenue visibility. The business is asset-light with an outsized cash balance, which has become a source of meaningful interest income.

**Key people (per the insider filings):** Alex Karp (CEO), Stephen Cohen (President), Shyam Sankar (CTO), David Glazer (CFO), Ryan Douglas (Officer / Head of Commercial), Alex Moore (Director), Lauren Stat (Director), Eric Woersching (Director), Alexandra Schiff (Director), Peter Thiel (Director).

**Concentration/characteristic risks:** meaningful government-contract concentration and renewal timing (lumpy quarterly revenue recognition), founder control, and — as discussed below — a **structural gross-margin question as AI compute costs enter cost of revenue**.

## 8. Multi-Year Financial History & the Inflection Timeline

**Phase 1 — Hypergrowth, GAAP losses (2018–2021).** Revenue compounded ~37% annually to $1,542M, but FY2020 operating loss was -$1,174M (-107% margin) as the company sprinted into commercial enterprise and international expansion. Direct listing (Sept 2020) occurred with GAAP losses of ~$1.17B.

**Phase 2 — Deliberate margin investment (2022–2023).** Growth troughed at **+16.7% in FY2023** ($2,225M) — the worst deceleration in the company's public history — precisely as R&D and go-to-market spending hit the P&L. FY2023 was nonetheless the crossover year: **first GAAP operating profit ($120M) and first GAAP net income ($210M)**, EPS $0.09, OCF $712M. This is the classic "profitability-first, growth-second" setup that the market punished in 2023 and is now rewarding in reverse.

**Phase 3 — Re-acceleration (2024).** Revenue +28.8% to $2,866M; operating margin 10.8%; OCF $1,154M; FCF ~$1,141M. AIP was commercializing; Q4 2024 was a margin trough (1.3% operating margin on a 78.9% gross margin) as investment spending hit the P&L just before the 2025 inflection.

**Phase 4 — The inflection (2025).** Revenue **+56.1% to $4,475M**; gross margin 82.4%; operating income **$1,414M (31.6%)**; net income **$1,625M (36.3%)**; EPS **$0.63**; OCF **$2,134M**; equity +47.7% to $7,387M. Growth and profitability both re-accelerated for the first time — the definition of operating leverage.

**Phase 5 — Current phase: hypergrowth at scale (2026 YTD).** 9M 2026 revenue $5,881M (**+91.6%**), gross margin 84.8%, operating margin 46.8%, net margin 52.1%, OCF $3,320M, equity $11,228M. Sequentially, revenue has compounded at ~+17–20% per quarter for **seven consecutive quarters** (Q1'25 $884M → Q3'26 $2,313M, a 2.6x in six quarters) — an unusually clean, unbroken growth curve for a company this large.

**FY2026 framing (scenario, not guidance):** 9M 2026 actual $5,881M. At a +17% sequential Q4 (a conservative repeat of the recent run-rate), Q4 2026 ≈ $2,706M → **FY2026 ≈ $8,587M, roughly +92% YoY**. Even at +12% QoQ, FY2026 ≈ $8,470M (+89%).
